oneliner.t: Democratic congresswoman from Tucson, a former Pima County supervisor and longtime TUSD board member, who won the Sept. 23, 2025 special election to succeed her late father and was sworn in Nov. 12, 2025 after a seven-week delay; unopposed in the 2026 primary, she faces Republican Daniel Butierez for the third time on Nov. 3.

born.note: Exact date from Wikipedia only; Tucson upbringing confirmed by her campaign release.

hometown.t: Tucson, Arizona (south side; Pueblo High School)

upbringing.t: A lifelong Tucsonan who grew up with two sisters on the city's south side and graduated from Pueblo High School (1989, per Wikipedia). Her grandfather came from Mexico as a bracero in 1945; her father, Raúl Grijalva, represented the area in Congress until his death in March 2025 — his record is his own. She earned a political science degree at the University of Arizona, directed the Pima County Teen Court diversion program for about 25 years, and was elected to the TUSD board in 2002. She is married to Sol Gómez, a librarian, and they have three children.

career.org: Pima County Teen Court (juvenile diversion; Pima Prevention Partnership benefit plan since 1996)

career.role: U.S. Representative, AZ-7 (Natural Resources; Education and the Workforce)

platform.t: Supports abolishing ICE, saying it cannot be reformed; no objection to border security or port-of-entry modernization; supports a permanent path to citizenship for DACA recipients.

Opposes the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship rules (says they burden people whose names changed through marriage); defends mail voting; does not trust federal control of elections and raised the prospect of ICE agents at polling places.
Supports single-payer Medicare for All; cosponsored the Medicare For All Act and a bill restoring ACA premium tax credits.
Accused the Israeli government of genocide in Gaza in a 2025 debate; cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act to halt certain military aid to Israel.

Criticized the Bureau of Reclamation for exempting Upper Basin states from Colorado River cuts; wants data centers to use waterless cooling; opposes the Oak Flat copper mine, citing San Carlos Apache concerns.

Fight 'Trump's economic chaos'; defend Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security and the VA; affordable housing; environmental justice; fully fund public education; humane immigration; tribal sovereignty; 'people-centered' foreign policy.

evidence.t: Her signature was the 218th, made after her Nov. 12, 2025 swearing-in; the House passed the bill 427–1 on Nov. 18.

complicating.t: The swearing-in was delayed about seven weeks; Democrats tied the delay to the petition, and Speaker Johnson denied any link. Arizona AG Kris Mayes sued Johnson on Oct. 21, 2025, and Grijalva joined the suit.

entries.t: As a supervisor, tried to add civilian and humanitarian-aid language to county Gaza resolutions; colleagues declined.

research_notes: FATHER: Raúl Grijalva's votes, money (FEC id H2AZ07070), committee record and his withdrawn 2021 amendment on the Gosar censure are his, not hers; none are attributed to her. 2025 SPECIAL: primary July 15, 2025 — Grijalva 61.5%, Deja Foxx 22.4%, Daniel Hernández Jr. 13.6%; general Sept. 23, 2025 — 68.9% (70,148) to Butierez 29.4% per Wikipedia (Ballotpedia shows 68.7%/64,041, likely an earlier count). Sworn in Nov. 12, 2025 after about 50 days; Speaker Johnson cited certification, recess and the shutdown and denied an Epstein link. 2026 primary: 59,304 votes, unopposed. Track AIPAC labels her as rejecting AIPAC. Photo not retrieved.
